question: How does Romans 8:1 fit into the "therefore" passages in Romans, and what does Romans 8 say that freedom looks like?

retrieved.section: Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
retrieved.text:
Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
    - Romans 3:20 is the “therefore” of condemnation - the whole world is guilty before God
    - Romans 5:1 is the “therefore” of justification
    - Romans 8:1 is the “therefore” of assurance
    - Romans 12:1 is the “therefore” of dedication
        - The basis for the other relationships that the author discussed in this section

retrieved.section: Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary — Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
retrieved.text:
Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary
Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
    - 8:1-4 - Freedom from Judgment (No condemnation)
    - 8:5-17 - Freedom from Defeat (No obligation; because we cannot save ourselves, submit to God)
    - 8:18-30 - Freedom from Discouragement (No Frustration)
    - 8:31-39 (No Separation)

retrieved.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Believers groan (23-25)
retrieved.text:
Believers groan (23-25)
    - We have a taste of glory to come, but anxious to get there
    - Adoption = redemption of body when Jesus comes back
        - There is a “climax” to adoption. The adoption begins when we are saved, the conversion when “the Spirit of adoption” comes and we receive the Holy Spirit. The “climax” is likened to the Rapture when we are called up and receive our glorified bodies
            - Example: When we are first saved, it is like an agreement to be adopted. The rapture and “climax” is when the child actually moving into the home
    - We as Believers still have hope as we know the climax of that adoption is coming

retrieved.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Holy Spirit groans (23-30) > The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
retrieved.text:
The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
    - We do not know God’s will or what to pray for, but the Spirit intercedes for us to “share the burden”. We are not only called to suffer with with Him, He shares our burden

answer: Romans 8:1 is the "therefore" of assurance [S1]. Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms: freedom from judgment (no condemnation) in verses 8:1-4 [S2], freedom from defeat (no obligation because we cannot save ourselves, submit to God) in verses 8:5-17 [S2], freedom from discouragement (no frustration) in verses 8:18-30 [S2], and freedom from separation in verses 8:31-39 [S2].
